name: Emergent Shapes - Ellipse
miniText: Can simple feedback recover a geometric constraint without directly drawing its equation? NetLogo Emergent Shapes Ellipse asks agents to approach positions whose distances to two fixed foci sum to a prescribed constant. Agents continue when their movement improves the constraint and choose a new direction when it worsens. Differential geometry [1] gives the curve context, computational geometry [2] supplies distance-based geometric reasoning, and Rosin's ellipse-fitting study [3] provides a contrasting numerical approach with its own normalization issues. The resulting point distribution illustrates decentralized search for a level set. Agent step size, stopping tolerance, initial positions, and random choices influence the approximation. This is a demonstration of constraint satisfaction, rather than evidence that natural elliptical forms arise by this rule or that every agent samples the ellipse uniformly.
